events.title: Repatriated as a US citizen
events.place: US District Court, Middle District of PA, Scranton
events.description: Card marked 'Rep.' (repatriation), vol. 1, certificate 250; country of birth U.S.A.; born Jan 5, 1897. US-born women who had married an alien before 22 Sep 1922 lost their citizenship and could regain it by repatriation.

bioAdditions: Grace's 1943 'naturalization' was in fact a repatriation. The index card is marked 'Rep.' and gives her country of birth as the U.S.A. (S1). Under the Expatriation Act of 1907, an American woman who married a foreigner took his nationality. Grace's husband Joseph DiBiasi was Italian-born, so she must have married him before the Cable Act took effect in September 1922, and she formally regained her citizenship in June 1943. In 1940 she and Joseph lived at 1015 Bunker Hill Street, where Grace, not Joseph, was the merchant running a general grocery store (S2). She was carrying on the grocery trade of her father John Petriello, whose store had stood at 1028 on the same street. She is very probably the 'Katie', 13, of the 1910 census (S3; see H0350).

openQuestionsResolved.question: (bio) naturalized 29 Jun 1943 - reason unknown
openQuestionsResolved.answer: Repatriation, not naturalization: the card is marked 'Rep.' and gives birth country U.S.A.; she had lost citizenship by marrying the Italian-born Joseph DiBiasi before Sept 1922.
